chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: The Black Cat in the Village with Kenny Clarke
summary: He and Lonnie Simmons joined a rhythm section at the Black Cat with Kenny Clarke, Fat Atkins and Frank Spearman.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, my thing was mostly -- you know, like after -- I would say after I left the Exclusive Club -- then I got this thing down in the Village, at the Black Cat.
Yeah.
That's where Lonnie went. That's where we went. We went down there. That's what happened. We got this job down in the Village working at the Black Cat.
You and Lonnie?
Me and Lonnie, Kenny Clarke, and his brother Frank, Fat Atkins...
What does he play?
Fat? He plays piano.
He did?
So we had piano, drums, guitar, and bass --
Who did you say the bass was?
Frank Clarke, Frank Spearmen in other words, I think he might have been a stepbrother of Kenny Clarke.
I see.
I don't know for sure, but I know his name was Frank Spearmen. And Lonnie Simmons.
So that was your first time in a group?
In really a big group.
And you were with a wonderful drummer?
Yes.
This was after Willie Gant.
This is after -- yeah. This is after Willie
Now that was another very good move then, wasn't it?
Oh, yeah.
It must have been a thrill for you to work with a real good drummer.
Yeah. Right.
Now, was Kenny Clarke considered a good drummer in those days? He must have been pretty good.
As far as being known is concerned, I don't know.
Yeah. But he was --
But he was a terrific drummer.
Yeah. Yeah.
Listen, we had -- we really had a thing going down there. We had a terrific rhythm section.
Was he a good bass player?
Yes. Yes he was.
So you had a wonderful rhythm section.
Oh yeah. We had -- we had -- (laugh).
I'll bet.
We really had it going down there.
